title: Derived operations on ringed pro-etale topoi
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small pro-etale sites and their size convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the induced inverse image and direct image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_V$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and fix an identification $c:u^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\sim}R_U$. For $T=U,V$ set $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$, using [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The module inverse image and direct image are
$$u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V,c}R_U,\qquad (u_*G)(W)=G(U\times_V W),$$
where the action on the latter is through the ring map $R_V\to u_*R_U$ adjoint to $c$, and tensor product is the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Here is the elementary module construction (the module-adjunction calculation in sites-modules.tex, label lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules). Write $L=u^{-1}$, $R=u_*$ on sheaves of sets, with unit $\eta$, and use their induced abelian and ring functors [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects, lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects]. Both preserve finite products. For $A=R_V$ and an $A$-module $F$, the action on $LF$ is $L\mu_F$ under $L(A\times F)\cong LA\times LF$; for an $LA$-module $N$, the $A$-action on $RN$ is $R\mu_N\circ(\eta_A\times1)$ under $R(LA\times N)\cong RLA\times RN$. The module axioms and linearity of maps follow by applying $L$ or $R$ to their defining equalities; restriction along the ring map $\eta_A$ gives the stated $A$-action. For an abelian map $\alpha:LF\to N$ with adjunct $\beta=R\alpha\circ\eta_F$, the adjuncts of $\alpha\circ L\mu_F$ and $\mu_N\circ(1\times\alpha)$ are respectively $\beta\circ\mu_F$ and $R\mu_N\circ(\eta_A\times\beta)$: use naturality $RL\mu_F\circ\eta_{A\times F}=\eta_F\circ\mu_F$ and $\eta_{A\times F}=\eta_A\times\eta_F$ under the product identifications. Injectivity of the set-sheaf adjunction on maps from $L(A\times F)$ shows that $\alpha$ is $LA$-linear if and only if $\beta$ is $A$-linear; its naturality restricts to give the module adjunction. Finally change scalars along $c$: the natural isomorphism from $LF\otimes_{LA,c}R_U$ to $LF$ with action $r\cdot m=c^{-1}(r)m$ is $m\otimes r\mapsto c^{-1}(r)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Their composites are identities by the tensor balancing relation, and their section maps commute with restrictions, so they give inverse sheaf maps. This identifies the displayed module pullback and direct-image actions with the preceding adjoint pair. The inverse image is exact: forgetting its module action gives the exact inverse image on abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], and kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have the corresponding underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Extension along the ring isomorphism $c$ just transports the action.

Define $Lu^*$ to be the triangulated functor induced by this exact functor applied termwise [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. In particular, for any K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $Lu^*K$ is represented by $u^*P$; the map $u^*P\to u^*K$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness. No functorial choice of K-flat resolutions is needed in this identified-coefficient case.

Choose functorial K-injective resolutions $K\to I(K)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] in the category of all $R_U$-module sheaves and define $Ru_*K=Q(u_*I(K))$, and $Ru_*(Qh)=Q(u_*I(h))$, with $Q$ the localization. This factors through $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_U)$: a quasi-isomorphism $h$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $I(h)$ between K-injectives, hence a homotopy equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the additive termwise functor $u_*$ preserves its homotopy inverse, so $Q(u_*I(h))$ is invertible. The resolution construction is triangulated [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. These are the ordinary, uncompleted unbounded derived operations
$$Lu^*:D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V)\longrightarrow D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_U),\qquad Ru_*:D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_U)\longrightarrow D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V),$$
with $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$: apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_U)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R_V)$, $F=u_*$ and $G=u^*$. Both total derived functors are everywhere defined by the preceding constructions, so its canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V)}(M,Ru_*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_U)}(Lu^*M,K)$, functorial in $M$ and $K$, gives the adjunction.

proof.text: For the canonical module-adjunction normalization, construct the tensor Hom equivalence on the existing change-of-rings presheaf [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Transpose sectionwise by ModuleCat.ExtendRestrictScalarsAdj.homEquiv; restrictions commute by the pure-tensor restriction formula and linearity. The two sectionwise inverse laws give inverse module morphisms. Compose with PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction to obtain the sheaf Hom equivalence. Its value at m is h applied to the sheafification unit of 1 tensor m. Prove naturality in the source by naturality of the sheafification unit and ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.map_tmul; target naturality is sectionwise composition.

Use the concrete AsSmall transport functors and model ring unit [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The correspondence from maps out of proEtaleModuleFromModel to maps into proEtaleModuleToModel is evaluation along AsSmall.down, with inverse evaluation along AsSmall.up. These are inverse on each section. After the model pullback-pushforward Hom equivalence (SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction), transport its output to the original direct-image module by evaluation along AsSmall.up. The ring action is precisely the action through the unit followed by c.hom. Compose these bijections with the tensor Hom equivalence from the previous step. Prove both naturality laws using the model adjunction naturality and sectionwise transport.

Apply Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv to the natural Hom equivalences. The intermediate map g is the transported tensor transpose, so its section formula is exactly the required tensor-unit normalization. For uniqueness, take h to be the identity on the pullback of M. Any other normalized adjunction gives a map g equal to this explicit map by sectionwise extensionality. Its Hom transpose therefore agrees with the constructed transpose. By Adjunction.homEquiv_id these transposes are the units. NatTrans.ext and Adjunction.ext give equality of adjunctions. The existing module and derived adjunction definitions are retained verbatim; deriving uses Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction.

For the arbitrary constant-ring specialization, let T be the identity object of the pro-etale site of Y. It is terminal, and proEtaleBaseChange f preserves its terminality by its published finite-limit preservation [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Direct image followed by evaluation at T is definitionally evaluation at its base change. Compose constantSheafAdj on Y with proEtaleSheafAdjunction and transport the right adjoint by this identity natural isomorphism. The resulting left adjoint is constant sheaf on Y followed by inverse image. Compare it with constantSheafAdj on X at the base-changed terminal object using Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. These are the constant-sheaf and sheafification adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

Identify the component of that uniqueness isomorphism with proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap by injectivity of the composite Hom equivalence. Adjunction.homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app identifies the comparison transpose with the constant-sheaf unit on X. Unfolding the specified coefficient map and cancelling the inverse-image Hom equivalence gives proEtaleConstantDirectImageMap. Unfolding this map and cancelling the sheafification Hom equivalence gives the constant presheaf section at the base-changed T. The explicit units of constantPresheafAdj and sheafificationAdjunction give exactly the same unit on X. Thus the specified map equals the isomorphism component and is invertible. No finiteness, nonemptiness, or topology on the coefficient ring is used.

split_report.summary: Made all module and derived-category notions explicit. Replaced the etale-only K-injective dependency by the existing general ringed-site resolution definitions and existence theorem; cited existing exact localization, K-injective comparison, triangulated right derivation and abstract derived adjunction. Wrote the underived module actions and both directions of linearity directly using the existing finite-product adjunction theorem; no new node is needed. The coefficient identification makes pullback exact, so termwise descent defines the same K-flat-computed functor without a functorial K-flat choice. All original derived functor types and the adjunction are retained. No completion or condensed coefficient identification is made. Maintainer citation repair: use the correctly typed canonical bifunctorial bijection of lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general in the final clause.
